profile.reading:
The address on file for this entry corresponds to a Chick-fil-A restaurant's hiring and training center in Shelby Charter Township, Macomb County, Michigan, on Schoenherr Road. A hiring center of this kind is a site where a restaurant recruits, interviews, and trains prospective employees; it is standard practice for busy Chick-fil-A locations to set aside space, sometimes a separate suite or trailer near the restaurant, for recruiting events distinct from the dining and kitchen areas customers see.

Nothing in the public record ties this address to data-center, colocation, telecommunications, or computing infrastructure of any kind. The operator name on file is an individual rather than a company, which is also inconsistent with how data-center operators are typically identified, and no technology, hosting, or infrastructure business could be found associated with that name at this location.

This entry does not describe an operating data center, and no technical specifications, power, cooling, square footage, or otherwise, are published here for that simple reason: there are none to publish. The most likely explanation is that this location was picked up in error from a mapping source that combines many kinds of points of interest, and a restaurant hiring center was mistakenly carried into a data-center listing. It remains recorded here for transparency rather than silently dropped, but a reader looking for data-center infrastructure at this address will not find any.

reading:
This record is a mapping artefact, and the honest page for it is an account of how it arose rather than a profile of a data centre operator. Dennis Sampier is a person, not a company. The single facility row beneath this name is an OpenStreetMap node created on 19 April 2021 and never edited since. It carries exactly three tags, a name reading Chick-fil-A Hiring Center, an operator field reading Dennis Sampier, and a telecom tag set to data_center. There is no building, no land use, no address, no website and no second version.

The changeset that created the node is the tell. Its comment is the single word sidewalks, it contains 33 changes, and it was made in the iD editor working over Bing aerial imagery. The contributor was tracing footpaths in a suburban commercial strip and dropped a point of interest along the way. The telecom classification is almost certainly a mis-selected preset in the editor's category list, and once applied it was never reviewed, because nothing about the node ever changed again.

The location, 42.6279 north and 82.9884 west, sits off Schoenherr Road in Shelby Charter Township, Macomb County, Michigan, in the 48315 postal area. The registry stores the city as Macomb County, which is a county rather than a municipality, another sign that the row was assembled from coordinates rather than from an address. A Chick-fil-A hiring centre is a temporary recruitment office that a franchisee runs in the weeks before a new restaurant opens, and Dennis Sampier is a local Chick-fil-A franchise operator. Neither is computing infrastructure. There is no data hall here, no power service, no generator, no cabinet and no company to profile.

The reason this belongs on the public record rather than being quietly deleted is that it shows precisely how facility counts inflate. The operator field in OpenStreetMap is free text and is frequently used for a proprietor's personal name, which is entirely correct practice for a shop or a restaurant. A pipeline that harvests every object carrying a data centre telecom tag and then groups those objects by their operator string will turn one mis-clicked preset into a facility, and the person named in the operator field into an operator with a facility count of one. Neither exists, and a page built on that basis would have to invent every number on it.

No capacity, address, ownership or date is recorded for this record because none can honestly be recorded. The correct disposition is removal of both the facility row and this operator entry, and the correct upstream fix is a note to the OpenStreetMap contributor that the telecom tag on that node is wrong.
